criterion: Spec 146 success criterion 12b — the five delivery semantics
gates: Criterion 13 (mailbox deletion) depends on this. If any property fails, the mailbox stays.

scenarios.scenario: 1: messages to one builder are delivered in the order sent
scenarios.stateMeaning: Ran against a live pinned server and passed.
scenarios.comparedAgainst: the server's own event log, in sequence order
scenarios.note: ten concurrent sends arrived in send order, checked against the server event log

scenarios.scenario: 2: a message sent during an active turn is queued and delivered on settle
scenarios.stateMeaning: Ran against a live pinned server and passed.
scenarios.note: ten messages sent during a live turn reached the server ZERO times before settle, then arrived in order — none lost, none interleaved

scenarios.scenario: 3: the acknowledgement means the server accepted it durably
scenarios.stateMeaning: Ran against a live pinned server and passed.
scenarios.verifiedOver: a second connection replaying the thread from sequence 0
scenarios.note: the receipt names server acceptance and nothing else; the message is in the server's log as read back by a connection that did not send it

scenarios.scenario: 4: a retry under the same idempotency key delivers once
scenarios.stateMeaning: Ran against a live pinned server and passed.
scenarios.note: the same key derived the same commandId from two independent journals, and the server's log holds exactly one delivery

scenarios.scenario: 5: with the server unreachable, a send fails loudly at the call site
scenarios.stateMeaning: Ran against a live pinned server and passed.
scenarios.note: the send threw at the call site within a bounded time and nothing was left holding the message — the mailbox's hold-and-retry is deliberately not reproduced

limits.scope: One thread against one freshly created server. These scenarios establish the five delivery semantics of success criterion 12b and nothing beyond them.
limits.scheduled: Durable scheduled delivery is covered by unit tests against a real on-disk store with an injected clock, NOT here: the property is "a pre-due message survives a restart", and demonstrating it live would mean holding a server for the length of a real delay. The store is the same fsynced append-only shape as the dispatch journal, which IS exercised live in Phase 3 scenarios E and F.
limits.ordering: Ordering is checked against the server's own event log in sequence order, not against the order the client believes it sent. A client-side list would pass against a queue that reordered on the wire.
limits.readReceipts: No scenario claims the AGENT read anything. Criterion 12b is about the server accepting durably, and the receipt type is named so that the stronger claim cannot be made by accident.
